card.text: A cluster of galaxies 776 million parsecs away whose gravity bends the light of the galaxies behind it.

sources.label: Planck Collaboration (2020), Planck 2018 results VI, A&A 641, A6; Astropy Planck18

sources.locator: caption: Abell 1689 bends and warps the space around it, affecting how light from objects behind the cluster travels

introduction.text: Hubble's view in visible and near-infrared light. The blue streaks are galaxies far behind the cluster, distorted by its gravity; the picture is flat and has no depth.

sources.label: ESA/Hubble heic1317a: NASA, ESA, the Hubble Heritage Team (STScI/AURA), J. Blakeslee (NRC Herzberg Astrophysics Program, Dominion Astrophysical Observatory), and H. Ford (JHU)
sources.locator: caption: the electric blue streaks are the distorted forms of galaxies that lie behind the cluster

optical.title: Abell 1689 in visible light
optical.summary: Hubble's visible and near-infrared view of the cluster and its lensed arcs. A flat picture of the sky, with no depth.
